name: 4-Ingredient Chocolate Crinkle Cookies

ingredients.name: melted unsalted butter, such as vegetable oil

instructions.primary_message: In a large bowl, whisk together butter and egg until smooth. Whisk in brownie mix and stir until mixture forms a dough and no dry flour pockets remain. Cover and refrigerate until chilled and no longer sticky to the touch, about 30 minutes.
While dough chills, adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 350°F. Line 2 rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper; set aside. Place confectioners' sugar in a medium bowl.

Using a #60 cookie scoop or large spoon, scoop 12 heaping 1-tablespoon-size portions of dough and roll each between damp hands until smooth. Dredge dough balls in confectioners' sugar, generously coating and gently pressing to help the sugar adhere (do not shake off excess). Arrange the 12 coated dough balls on one prepared baking sheet, spacing them about 2 inches apart.

Bake cookies until puffed and cracked and edges have begun to set but centers are still soft (cookies will look raw between cracks and seem underdone), about 10 minutes, rotating sheet halfway through baking. Cool cookies on sheet for 5 minutes; transfer to a wire rack and cool completely, about 15 minutes.

While the first batch bakes, scoop and roll 12 more dough portions, coat them in powdered sugar, and arrange on the second prepared sheet. Continue baking cookies in batches of 12 at a time, keeping the remaining dough covered and refrigerated between batches, until all cookies are baked (you should have about 46 to 48 cookies total).

schema_metadata.keywords: crinkle cookies, christmas cookies recipe, chocolate crinkle cookies, 4-ingredient-chocolate-crinkle-cookies

description: Make these easy 4-ingredient chocolate crinkle cookies with a clever shortcut: boxed brownie mix. Chewy, fudgy, and dusted in confectioners' sugar, they're the fastest way to bakery-worthy holiday cookies.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 hr 11 min.

Optional substitutions: melted unsalted butter → neutral oil

Notes: In recipe testing, Julia preferred Ghirardelli Dark Chocolate Brownie Mix, but any good-quality brownie mix will work here—just make sure it's rich and chocolatey. Depending on the brand, you may need to refrigerate the dough a bit longer than directed to reach that firm-yet-malleable texture.

Make-ahead and storage: The dough can be prepared and refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 24 hours before rolling and baking.
Cookies can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week.
author: Leah Colins
